items.label: Elevation
items.desc: Mean height above the areoid (the Martian zero level).

items.label: Typical slope
items.desc: Median slope within the cell.
items.caveat: Slopes are measured across a baseline of about 3.7 km, the same on all three worlds. They describe regional relief and understate the slopes a lander or rover meets.

items.label: Steep-ground slope
items.desc: 90th-percentile slope: one tenth of the cell is steeper than this.
items.caveat: Slopes are measured across a baseline of about 3.7 km, the same on all three worlds. They describe regional relief and understate the slopes a lander or rover meets.

items.label: Roughness
items.desc: Spread of height left after removing the local tilt (inter-quartile range).

items.label: Laser-shot coverage
items.desc: Share of elevation bins in the cell that contain a real MOLA measurement; the rest are interpolated.

items.label: Annual mean
items.desc: Sol-weighted mean surface temperature over the Martian year.

items.label: Warmest afternoon
items.desc: Surface temperature at 14:00 local time in the warmest of six sampled seasons.

items.label: Coldest pre-dawn
items.desc: Surface temperature at 05:00 local time in the coldest of six sampled seasons.

items.label: Sunlight at the surface
items.desc: Annual mean of the day-and-night average solar flux on level ground, after dust and gas extinction.

items.label: Water-equivalent hydrogen
items.desc: Hydrogen in the top decimetres, expressed as if all of it were water.
items.caveat: May be ice or hydrated minerals. Not reported poleward of about 57°.

items.label: Surface pressure
items.res: model grid, adjusted to cell elevation
items.desc: Annual-mean pressure, corrected hydrostatically from the model's smoothed topography to this cell's MOLA elevation.
items.caveat: The seasonal CO₂ cycle moves pressure by roughly a quarter through the year.

items.label: Seasonal pressure swing
items.desc: Range between the highest and lowest seasonal pressure, relative to the annual mean.

items.label: Dust opacity, annual mean
items.desc: Visible optical depth of dust above the surface in a typical year.
items.caveat: Typical-year scenario. Global dust storms are excluded.

items.label: Dust opacity, dustiest season
items.desc: Highest seasonal-mean dust optical depth in a typical year.

items.label: Thermal inertia
items.desc: How slowly the ground heats and cools. Low values mean loose dust; high values mean rock or cemented soil.
items.caveat: The climate model's surface field, built from MGS-TES mapping and smoothed to the model grid.

items.label: Albedo
items.desc: Share of sunlight the bare ground reflects. Bright regions are dust-mantled.
items.caveat: The climate model's surface field, built from MGS-TES mapping.

items.label: Iron
items.desc: Iron in the top decimetres.

items.label: Silicon
items.desc: Silicon in the top decimetres; about 20 wt% is typical of basalt.

items.label: Potassium
items.desc: Potassium in the top decimetres.

items.label: Chlorine
items.desc: Chlorine in the top decimetres; elevated where salts or volcanic exhalations accumulated.

items.label: Thorium
items.desc: Thorium in the top decimetres.

dimensions.label: Terrain
dimensions.how: Median slope, steep-ground slope and roughness, each measured over a 3.7 km baseline on both worlds. Similarity falls to 0.61 when values differ by a factor of two and to 0.14 at a factor of four.

dimensions.label: Rock type
dimensions.how: Measured planetary chemistry is matched to the mapped Earth rock class with RADIUM's affinity table. The table is an expert judgement, not a measurement.
dimensions.note: Basaltic crust is assumed, as mapped across Mars (silicon 20.4 wt%, iron 15.1 wt%); chlorine 0.58 wt% raises the match to evaporites.

dimensions.label: Ice and frozen ground
dimensions.how: A 0–1 index of ice evidence at the planetary site is compared with a 0–1 index of frozen ground on Earth (permanent ice cover, or mean ground temperature from 0 °C down to −8 °C). Similarity = 1 − difference.
dimensions.note: Planetary index from thermal stability of shallow ground ice (annual mean 198 K or colder) and water-equivalent hydrogen, which counts only where ice is stable. Earth index from permanent ice cover and mean ground temperature.

dimensions.label: Bare, dry ground
dimensions.how: How much of the Earth cell is exposed rock or soil (not hidden by plants or glacier ice; vegetation index full credit at 0.10 or below, none at 0.35) and how dry it is (precipitation full credit at 60 mm/yr or below, none at 600 mm/yr). The same test for every planetary site.

dimensions.label: Ground temperature
dimensions.how: Annual-mean ground temperature on both worlds, Gaussian with a 40 K tolerance: an Earth site 40 K warmer than the Mars site scores 0.61. Mars is colder than almost anywhere on Earth, so this rewards the coldest ground. Not scored for the Moon.

dimensions.label: Airborne dust
dimensions.how: Visible optical depth of airborne dust on Mars against aerosol optical depth on Earth. The quantity is the same; particle size, composition and air density are not.

breaks_down.label: Gravity
breaks_down.text: Earth's gravity is 2.6 times stronger. Loads, traction, dust settling and human movement all differ.

breaks_down.label: Air pressure
breaks_down.text: The air here is about 105 times denser than at the Mars site. Wind forces, heat transfer, parachutes and boiling points cannot be reproduced outdoors.

breaks_down.label: Radiation
breaks_down.text: With no global magnetic field and little or no air, surface radiation is far higher than anywhere on Earth. RADIUM holds no radiation dataset and does not score it.

breaks_down.label: Water and life
breaks_down.text: This Earth cell has 34 mm of precipitation a year and a peak vegetation index of 0.09. Liquid water, weathering and microbes alter rock and soil in ways that have no counterpart at the planetary site.

breaks_down.label: Length of day
breaks_down.text: Close to Earth's, one of the few conditions that nearly matches.

protocol.instrument_class: Rover or mobility test article with wheel odometry, inertial sensors and stereo or depth cameras.
data_to_collect: Terrain photographs and local slope measurements per segment
protocol.comparison: Plot slip and stall rate against measured slope, then compare those slopes with the 13 km NW of Gediz Vallis, in Aeolis Mons on Mars target's typical and steep-ground slope values.
protocol.informative_outcome: Slip-versus-slope curves measured here can bound expected performance on 13 km NW of Gediz Vallis, in Aeolis Mons on Mars slopes within the compared range; behaviour outside that range is untested.
protocol.laboratory_needs: Lower gravity changes wheel loading and slip; scale results with reduced-gravity models or offloading tests before applying them.

preparation: Site access and permits: not assessed. Many analog sites are protected areas, private land or research reserves and need permission.
Conservation rules: not assessed. Check protected-area and heritage restrictions before any sampling or vehicle use.
Transport and logistics: not assessed. Distances in RADIUM are straight-line and say nothing about roads or travel time.
Field safety: plan for local hazards such as heat, cold, altitude, isolation and terrain; RADIUM does not assess them.
Some planetary conditions (vacuum, low gravity, radiation, extreme cold) can only be simulated in laboratory facilities.
